title: Jos Buttler Becomes the Highest Run-Scorer in T20 Cricket History
excerpt: The England wicketkeeper-batter overtakes Kieron Pollard to claim the all-time T20 record with 14,833 runs, capping a remarkable 2026 that has spanned the IPL, international cricket, and The Hundred.
body:
• Jos Buttler has become the highest run-scorer in T20 cricket history, surpassing Kieron Pollard's tally of 14,803 runs during The Hundred 2026 to reach 14,833 runs across 492 innings.
  • The England wicketkeeper-batter first overtook Chris Gayle on July 24 during Manchester Super Giants' match against London Spirit at Lord's, then closed the remaining 231-run gap to Pollard within two weeks.
  • Buttler's record has been built across franchise cricket worldwide—the IPL with Gujarat Titans, The Hundred, the SA20, and 160 T20 internationals for England—making him the format's most prolific batter at 36 years old.
  • Indian stars Virat Kohli (14,218 runs) and Rohit Sharma (12,531 runs) rank sixth and tenth respectively on the all-time T20 list, with Kohli the only active player within realistic striking distance of the top five.

From Second to First in a Fortnight

Jos Buttler's ascent to the top of T20 cricket's all-time run charts has been swift and decisive. The England wicketkeeper-batter overtook Chris Gayle to claim second place on July 24 during The Hundred 2026, scoring 16 runs off 11 balls for the Manchester Super Giants against London Spirit at Lord's. That knock moved him to 14,572 runs, ten clear of Gayle's career total of 14,562.

With only 231 runs separating him from Kieron Pollard's record, Buttler maintained his momentum through The Hundred's group stage, crossing Pollard's mark of 14,803 to reach 14,833 runs in 492 innings, according to ESPNcricinfo data updated on August 5.

The record caps a remarkable year for the 36-year-old. After a difficult 2026 T20 World Cup, where he struggled for rhythm, Buttler rediscovered his form during the IPL, scoring 526 runs for Gujarat Titans and helping the franchise reach the final.

The Numbers Behind the Record

Buttler's achievement is distinguished as much by efficiency as by volume. He has reached 14,833 runs in just 492 innings, compared to Pollard's 14,803 in 663 innings—a difference that underscores Buttler's consistently higher scoring rate. His career strike rate of 146.74 sits comfortably above Pollard's 151.02 for power, but Buttler averages 35.48 per dismissal against Pollard's 31.76, meaning he combines sustained scoring with explosive hitting.

The Englishman has nine T20 centuries and 106 half-centuries across his career, spanning franchise leagues on four continents. His highest T20 score, 131 off 64 balls, came in the fifth T20I against India at the Rose Bowl in Southampton, a knock that featured 12 fours and eight sixes and sealed a 4-0 series win for England.

"Buttler is the most complete white-ball batter in the world. He can anchor and he can destroy, and he does both better than anyone I've seen."

— Nasser Hussain, former England captain and Sky Sports commentator

A Global Career Like No Other

What sets Buttler apart from his predecessors at the top of the list is the breadth of his career. Gayle's T20 runs were accumulated largely in the Caribbean Premier League and the IPL. Pollard's came across a staggering 746 matches, many in lower-profile leagues.

Buttler, by contrast, has been a consistent performer across the world's most competitive T20 environments. He is the leading run-scorer in the history of the IPL among overseas players, a multiple-time champion in The Hundred, and England's all-time highest T20I run-scorer with 4,212 runs in 160 internationals. He is also the first wicketkeeper-batter to reach 4,000 T20I runs, a milestone he achieved during the 2026 T20 World Cup in Kolkata.

His three-year contract extension with Lancashire, signed earlier this year, ensures he will continue playing domestic T20 cricket in England alongside his franchise commitments in India and South Africa.

Where India's Stars Stand

For Indian cricket fans, the all-time T20 leaderboard remains a point of pride. Virat Kohli sits sixth with 14,218 runs at an average of 42.22—the highest among the top ten—with 10 centuries and 110 half-centuries. Kohli's scoring has been concentrated in the IPL, where he is the league's all-time leading run-scorer for Royal Challengers Bengaluru.

Rohit Sharma occupies tenth place with 12,531 runs, though both he and Kohli have retired from T20 internationals following India's 2024 T20 World Cup triumph. Both continue to add to their tallies through the IPL.

What's Next

Buttler's immediate focus remains The Hundred 2026, where Manchester Super Giants are pushing for a place in the knockout rounds. With franchise leagues around the world expanding their calendars, the 36-year-old shows no signs of slowing down. The question is no longer whether Buttler will hold the record, but how far he will extend it before he finally hangs up his gloves.
